strengths: The paper makes a genuine theoretical contribution: it generalizes the rank-one-update/Cauchy-matrix relationship between eigenbases (previously established only for path graphs and restricted eigenvalue/update conditions in Fernández-Menduiña et al. 2025) to arbitrary symmetric matrices and arbitrary hierarchical graph partitions, via the introduction of Cauchy factors and a deflation procedure to handle repeated eigenvalues and orthogonal updates (Theorem 3.1, Lemma 3.1, Appendix C-D).

A clear and rigorous complexity analysis is provided (Theorem 3.2), showing the factorization can be computed in O(kn^2 + sum f_i(n)) sequentially or O(kn^2 + max f_i(n)) in parallel, which is a meaningful improvement over the O(n^3) cost of dense eigendecomposition when the interface size k is small relative to n.

The paper goes beyond pure theory to propose practical algorithms for finding good partitions (greedy balanced-cut heuristic guided by the theoretical cost function) and for handling unfavorable partitions via localized spectral sparsification, with an accompanying theoretical guarantee (Theorem 4.1) on spectral distortion.

Synthetic experiments carefully isolate and confirm the predicted quadratic scaling in n and linear scaling in k, and show negligible preprocessing overhead, providing solid empirical support for the theoretical claims.

The interpretability experiment (Grad-CAM cumulative node contribution, Figure 5) is a nice qualitative validation that the method indeed induces a more localized inductive bias compared to global GFT and attention-based Polynormer, connecting the theoretical construction to an observable property of the trained model.

L2G-Net achieves competitive accuracy with dramatically fewer learnable parameters than transformer-based SOTA methods (Figure 4), which is a practically relevant contribution for resource-constrained settings.
weaknesses: The real-world GNN evaluation uses only a single level of hierarchy (L=1, partitioning into two subgraphs) per Section 6.2, which undercuts the paper's central narrative of a deep hierarchical local-to-global architecture; the multi-level scaling story (e.g., L=log n) is validated only for raw factorization runtime on synthetic graphs, not for actual downstream GNN performance or end-to-end runtime in the real experiments.

Empirical gains on real datasets are mixed and often within error bars of competing methods (e.g., Amazon-Ratings accuracy is below CO-GNN, Polynormer, and MP-SSM in Table 1/5; Roman-Empire and Tolokers results overlap substantially with Stable-ChebNet's confidence intervals), making the claim of the method "outperforming existing spectral techniques" and being "competitive with the state-of-the-art" only weakly supported by statistically robust margins.

The runtime comparison in Table 2 is only against full dense eigendecomposition, which is a strawman that no practical spectral GNN actually uses; a more informative comparison would include end-to-end training/inference time versus polynomial filters, MPNNs, and Polynormer, which is missing.

The evaluation is confined to the four heterophilous datasets from a single benchmark suite (Platonov et al., 2023), all of modest size (≤ ~25k nodes); no evaluation on established long-range benchmarks (e.g., LRGB) despite the paper's motivation being explicitly about capturing long-range dependencies, and no evidence of scalability to substantially larger graphs where the claimed complexity benefits would matter more.

The paper does not report or analyze the actual interface sizes k, partition quality, or achieved factorization speed-versus-approximation trade-off in the real GNN experiments beyond a single sparsification ratio per dataset (Table 3/4), leaving open how sensitive downstream performance is to these key hyperparameters, and no ablation isolates the contribution of the hierarchical/Cauchy design versus other architectural choices (e.g., filter sharing, RBF/spline basis choice, ODE-inspired residual formulation borrowed from Hariri et al. 2025).

No mention of code release, and given the complexity of the algorithm (deflation, secular equation solving, hierarchical bookkeeping in Algorithm 2/3), reproducibility from the paper text alone would be challenging without released implementation.

The worst-case behavior when good hierarchical partitions do not exist (large interface size, e.g., dense graphs like Tolokers where k after sparsification is still 25) is acknowledged but not deeply analyzed; the paper does not clearly delineate the class of real-world graphs for which the method's asymptotic advantages actually materialize versus degrade to near-cubic behavior.
